title: Close the gap between the status page and its design
summary: The status page was rebuilt on the new design but never actually compared against it, so the binder's name lost its masthead to an accordion header, the page ended up with no headings at all, the cards drifted to a different typeface, and the design's rectangular corner radii never reached the stylesheet at all. This binder fixes what is wrong, writes down the three places the page differs on purpose, and puts the design comparison into the checks so it can never be skipped again.
motivation: The previous binder intended design fidelity but never gated it — ten items carried a design reference and not one carried a visual check, so nothing ever opened the design.

the generated Codex mirrors of that file under .agents/skills/ and plugins/karta/

a second viewport or the dark theme in the comparison; this binder validates one view. Recorded so the deferral reads as a decision rather than an oversight: the design does carry two width breakpoints. At max-width:880px it collapses the two-column shell and unsticks the rail, giving it max-width:392px (export 53-56). At max-width:640px it narrows both the header row and the main grid to an 18px gutter and steps every binder headline from 40px down to 32px (export 57-60) — the only font-size declaration inside its whole style block and its only responsive type step. None of that is built or compared here; it is the obvious next binder.

design_facts.stack: Python stdlib http.server + vendored Vue 3 SPA, shipped as a Claude Code / Codex plugin skill

token_manifest.mechanism: A PAGE-SIDE fact, not a design fact — it sat in this block presented as design-derived and it is not. The page's theme cascade is four selectors: bare :root, an @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) override, and both data-theme selectors (serve_status.py:1086-1089 on karta/watch-redesign/integration). That is what makes the system default and the forced ?theme=light|dark override both work, and the comparison depends on the forced override because the comparison tool has no theme input of its own. The design does NOT work this way: it declares two selectors, ':root, :root[data-theme="light"]' (export 15) and ':root[data-theme="dark"]' (export 27), and zero prefers-color-scheme rules anywhere in 940 lines (export 15) — its only three media queries are prefers-reduced-motion and the two width breakpoints (export 50, 53, 57). The page keeps its four selectors and this binder does not touch them: dropping the preference query would make the page ignore the reader's operating-system setting, which is a regression the design cannot ask for.
token_manifest.source_of_truth: the design's own 27 custom properties, as recorded fact by fact in design_fact_table with an export line on each. Both of the design's palette blocks define the identical 27 names — light at export 16-25, dark at export 28-37 (export 16, 15). The page's 27-token table in serve_status.py matched all of them exactly in both themes at the time of the comparison, and this binder changes no value; the palette check reads against the recorded design values rather than against the stylesheet it is inspecting, so it cannot pass by agreeing with itself.
token_manifest.no_new_tokens: the comparison matched all 27 tokens exactly in light and dark. No token is added, changed or removed anywhere in this binder, which is why every item's token_changes is absent or empty.

type_roles.basis: rebuilt from design_fact_table. The earlier version said the serif was 'titles only ... the work-item card's title at the 19px step' and gave IBM Plex Sans 'body text, controls and page chrome'. The export contradicts both: 19px is declared zero times in the file (export 290), and the header and rail declare IBM Plex Sans zero times between them (export 66, 97). What follows are inventories with line numbers, not a doctrine.
type_roles.Newsreader: six jobs in the export, not one: the 40px binder-title headings (export 256, 430, 482, 661, 841), the 25px wave numerals (export 276, 331, 380, 435, 485, 593, 630, 664, 794), the 24px next-action prose sentence (export 240, 469), the 21px wordmark (export 70), the 20px work-item card title — 27 declarations, first at export 290 — and the 17px rail binder names (export 121, 144, 174, 197, 213). A titles-only role does not describe it: the 24px element is a full prose sentence with an italic run inside it, not a title (export 240).
type_roles.IBM Plex Sans: body copy, and almost entirely by inheritance. The body rule names the family once (export 40) and the text that uses it does not re-declare it — the card descriptions at 13.5px (export 291, 346) and the binder description at 16.5px (export 257) both inherit it, and the description being sans is the exact opposite of what this binder used to claim. The only element that names the sans outright is the next-action band's Copy button, and it does so in both of the bands the export draws — three declarations of the family in the whole file, the body rule and those two buttons (export 40, 243, 472). It is not the chrome family: the header declares font-family five times as mono and zero times as sans (export 66), and the rail declares mono 29 times and sans zero (export 97).
type_roles.IBM Plex Mono: the chrome family — eyebrows, slugs, chips, counts, state labels, file paths, git refs, both wave-header labels and the footer. Its two dominant steps are 10px and 11px, tied at 99 declarations each and together nearly two thirds of the file's 323 font-size declarations (export 74, 79).

token_manifest.available_weights: IBM Plex Sans and Mono at 400, 500 and 600; Newsreader at 400 and 500. Eight vendored faces, no other weight exists, and none is added.
token_manifest.motion_rule: every karta keyframe already has a reduced-motion settling, and the check that enforces it derives the keyframe set from the stylesheet rather than from a hand-kept list, so a keyframe added without a settling fails on its own.

design_fact_table.why_here: design_facts is additionalProperties:false in skills/karta-plan/references/binder-schema.json and admits only source and stack, so a fact table cannot legally live there. token_manifest is typed [object,null] with no property schema, so this is where the binder can carry a free-form design record. Nothing else in the binder gained a key.
design_fact_table.source: the byte-exact Claude Design export 'Karta Watch.dc.html', 940 lines, imported from claude-design://59832c82-69dc-4841-9c45-c4a8a86730a3. Every line number below is a line in THAT file, not in the committed capture at docs/designs/karta-watch-1440x900-light.html and not in serve_status.py.
design_fact_table.rule: a design fact is only a fact if it carries an export line number. Any number about the design that cannot be cited to a line in the export must not be written into this binder. Four review rounds read the binder and none opened the export, which is how '16px base step', '19px card title' and 'five headed sections' survived; this table exists so the fifth mistake of that kind is caught by reading one block.
design_fact_table.status_key: declared = the export writes this literally on that line. computed = the export does not write this value; it is arithmetic over declared values, and the declared inputs are named in the fact. absent = the export declares this property nowhere, and the fact says so explicitly because several binder claims rest on values the design never wrote.
settled_collisions: band height: the header's inner row DECLARES height:70px (export 67); the next-action band declares no height at all (export 238). Two different elements, one shared word. Kept both, under distinct ids header-inner-row and band-height-absent.
progress bar: the rail card's bar is height:4px (export 151) and the binder panel's summary bar is height:6px (export 259). Kept both, as rail-bar-* and panel-bar-*.

hatch stops: the rail bar remainder and the legend swatch both use repeating-linear-gradient(135deg,var(--now) 0 2px,transparent 2px 6px) (export 153, 227), while the panel summary bar uses 2px 7px (export 261). Read all three lines directly; the 6px/7px difference is real and both are kept.
card title size: the rail's binder name is 17px (export 121) and the work-item card's title is 20px (export 290). Extractors used the same label for both. Kept as rail-card-title and card-title.

card grid floor: the notif panel's waves use minmax(320px,1fr) (export 282, 337, 386) and the winpar/wingates panels use minmax(300px,1fr) (export 491, 599, 636, 670, 761, 800). The design has no single floor; kept both.

duplicated absences: body-font-size-absent, font-size-16px-absent and the 19px absence were each reported by three or more extractors. Deduplicated to one fact apiece, each verified by grep over all 940 lines (font-size:16px = 0 hits, font-size:19px = 0 hits, 323 font-size declarations across 14 values, none of them 16 or 19).
design_fact_table.unreconciled: RECONCILED. Every claim this table contradicted has been rewritten in place: token_manifest.type_roles and token_manifest.mechanism above, the scope's viewport exclusion, and six work items — heading-outline, card-lead-and-disclosure, panel-nesting, type-fidelity, band-geometry-and-wave-rhythm and summary-line-and-now-emphasis — plus the closing gate. Two changes came out of that pass and are not corrections of a design fact: binder-masthead's visual oracle was demoted to unit because no channel exists to scope a visual gate to one region of the page, and a tenth item, container-shape-language, was added from this table's radius data. The rule stands going forward: where a work item and this table disagree, the table wins, and a number about the design that carries no export line does not belong in this binder. One later change is neither a correction nor a consequence of this table and is recorded so it is not mistaken for one: the human revised the card item's decision after reading these facts, adding a halted card that opens at rest (export 305, 310, 313) and explicitly declining the sole-card case the same facts carry (export 448, 853). A decision changed there; no fact did.

contract.exposes: the fidelity record — every difference that is meant to stay, each with the reason it stays — kept in the same runbook the first item wrote, so the next comparison is read against it instead of re-litigating settled decisions

contract.scope: one view: the whole page at 1440 by 900 in light theme. The comparison tool validates one view per run, and a second viewport or the dark theme is not in this binder. One limit of the pinned view is stated here rather than left to surprise the comparison: item status derives only from git refs (karta_next.py _item_status returns done/failed/built/building solely from that item's git facts and otherwise only blocked/ready), and the fixture's slug matches no karta/<slug>/* ref, so every item in the compared view derives as pending. Nothing state-dependent — a halted card, an in-flight ring, a running strip, a part-filled progress bar — is observable in this comparison, and no assertion here may rest on one. Those treatments are checked where they actually can be, in the unit oracles of the items that add them. There is no caller channel that carries this item's intended differences into the comparison worker, and the earlier draft was wrong to name focus areas as one. karta-validate accepts oracle assertions and would emit an ACCEPTANCE verdict against them (skills/karta-validate/SKILL.md:35, 185), but nothing passes them: grepping for 'ACCEPTANCE' or 'oracle assertions' across skills/karta-build, skills/karta-verify and skills/karta-deliver returns zero hits. The loop's focus-area, navigation and viewport fields all come from DESIGN_VALIDATION_PARAMS, which exists only inside skills/karta-build/references/design-validation-loop.md (lines 26, 33-35, 38, 44, 118) and has no binder-side source. So the worker will report the intended differences as differences, the loop's own exit bar is zero critical and zero major over the WHOLE report at three rounds and then a halt to a human (skills/karta-build/references/design-validation-loop.md:3, 76), and reading that report against the list below is the human step this gate ends on. It is not something the tool can be told.
contract.residuals: small leftovers this comparison turns up are fixed here when they fall inside the findings this binder took on. Anything new and larger is written into the record as an open finding rather than quietly absorbed, so the binder does not grow at its own last step. The three intended differences are enumerated in this item's assertions rather than sourced from the record — the record is the human-readable mirror and the comparison worker never sees it — so a newly found major or critical difference fails this gate; landing it anyway is karta-deliver's accept decision, not a waiver this gate can write.
contract.differences_rechecked: all three intended differences were re-read against the export after this rework, and all three still hold as deliberate. (a) stands unchanged: the design's only headings are five binder titles, one per seeded panel (export 256, 430, 482, 661, 841), and its own script shows one panel at a time (export 909), so a rendered design view holds one heading while this page renders every binder at once. That narrowing is not something this comparison can see: the pinned fixture renders every item as pending, so no halted card appears in the compared view at all. It is proven in card-lead-and-disclosure's own unit oracle, which is where it belongs. (c) stands unchanged: the design draws no spine and no wrapper around its panel, which is a plain card with no width, max-width or margin of its own (export 249, 477), and the wrapper this page keeps carries the multi-repository hub context the design was never asked to model. There is no fourth: the next-action band's 16px radius and the command chip's edge are NOT intended differences and must not be written into the record as any — they are defects the ninth item repairs (export 238, 242), and if that item failed to land they surface here through the container shape assertion below, which fails on any container that has fallen back to square corners and on an edge still drawn at full strength.
contract.ruled_out: five differences were ruled out at plan time and must not be re-raised as defects: the design's five seeded binder panels — four of which declare display:none, with its own script showing exactly one at a time (export 237, 909) — against this repo's live binders; the single-item waves the real run produced; the absent copy control in a state that has no runnable command; token drift, since all 27 tokens matched exactly (export 15, 16); and the lane glyph, which the design builds from 2px-radius bar boxes (export 230, 332) and this page draws as an SVG icon with painted legend swatches, a divergence the page's own source booked before this binder existed (serve_status.py:669-674 on karta/watch-redesign/integration).
contract.serialization: every page item in this binder edits this same file, and that is expected — each one is serialized for it and merges before the next starts. There is no claim here that no later item touches it.
contract.verification_honesty: this is the only item in the binder with a visual oracle, and the only place anything is rendered. The nine items before it are all deterministic, including the masthead item, whose visual oracle was demoted because no channel exists to scope a visual gate to one region of the page — the reasoning is in that item's contract. Everything those nine proved was proven against rendered source and the page's own tables. That is the division on purpose: the fast deterministic checks own what can be read from the source, and this one owns what only a rendered page can settle — composition, hierarchy and density.
